'''Wayne Bowen''' is an American pharmacologist, biologist, and neuroscientist who is Professor Emeritus of Neuroscience, and Adjunct Professor of Neuroscience at [[Brown University]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Bowen, Wayne |url=https://vivo.brown.edu/display/wbowen |access-date=2025-07-08 |website=vivo.brown.edu |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://vivo.brown.edu/display/wbowen |title=Wayne Bowen |publisher=brown.edu |accessdate=January 27, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=Zk0ouhgAAAAJ&hl=en |title=Wayne Bowen |accessdate=January 27, 2017}}</ref>

Bowen earned his B.S. in chemistry from [[Morgan State College]] and completed a Ph.D. in biochemistry and neurobiology at [[Cornell University]] in 1981.<ref name=":0" /> 

He is a nationally recognized leader in research on sigma receptors and is generally credited with the discovery and initial characterization of the sigma-2 receptor.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-10-15 |title=Cognition Therapeutics Sponsoring Satellite Symposium on "Sigma-2 Receptors: Role in Health and Disease" during Society for Neuroscience Annual Meeting {{!}} Cognition Therapeutics, Inc. |url=https://ir.cogrx.com/press_releases/cognition-therapeutics-sponsoring-satellite-symposium-on-sigma-2-receptors-role-in-health-and-disease-during-society-for-neuroscience-annual-meeting/ |access-date=2025-07-08 |language=en-US}}</ref>
